scenario: nomad - audit what retains the cluster server before a lifecycle rework
score_rationale: Blast's retained_via_interfaces gave me the narrowed-interface holders — the exact high-risk set grep could not have produced — and the index_caveat hint correctly drove me to the fn-value gap (Q1/Q3), but I still needed ~6 read/grep fallbacks to recover exact field lines, verify which chains are runtime-wired, exclude EventBroker, and find the raftApplyFn shim (Q2), so it sits at the top of the 7-8 band rather than 9.
q4_value: The retained_via_interfaces list on the nomad.Server blast — it surfaced the 23 narrowed-interface holders (deploymentwatcher, drainer, volumewatcher, periodic, auth.Encrypter, allocrunner/allocwatcher/widmgr RPCer, HTTPServer, scheduler Planner chains) that have NO compile-time tie to *Server and that grep for '*Server' would have completely missed; this is the core of the audit and the highest-risk dead-handle set.
q5_improve: On retained_via_interfaces, distinguish runtime-wired chains from merely-declared containment paths — the config.Config.RPCHandler row asserted chain 'agent.Agent > nomad.Server' but in production that field is nil; flagging which chains have an actual assignment site (vs. a possible interface-satisfaction edge) would have saved a full-repo grep to separate live holders from dormant fields.
